subject: Using dynamic indexing in a particle filter

messages.subject: Using dynamic indexing in a particle filter
parts:
Dear developers & users.

I am trying to construct a simple particle filter for discrete states and observations. Specifically, for each time t, there are 3 arrows on a computer screen, with each arrow pointing either right or left. Then, a target appears on one side of the screen. One of the cues predicts the target with some high probability (e.g 75%), and the others point at random. The cues change roles from time to time, such that a previous cue becomes random and a new one becomes predictive of the target. 
In terms of the state-space model, this means that there are 3 possible discrete states, such that the probability of the state to continue to the next trial is defined as tau, and is a free parameter
The probability that the target will appear at the direction to which the relevant cue has pointed is gamma, which is also a free parameter.

Here is the model. The model is given the cues (a matrix of 3*T, with 1 indicating a right-pointing cue and -1 a left pointing cue), the targets (with 1 indicating a right target, and 0 a left target)
stateSpaceCode<-nimbleCode({
  gamma~dunif(0.51,0.99)
  tau~dunif(0.0001,0.9999)
 

  x[1]~dcat(lambda[1,1:3])
  lambda[1,1]<-1/3
  lambda[1,2]<-1/3
  lambda[1,3]<-1/3
  
  
  prob[1]<-equals(cues[1,x[1]],1)*gamma+equals(cues[1,x[1]],-1)*(1-gamma)
  
  target[1]~dbern(prob[1])
  
  for (t in 2:nTrials){
    x[t]~dcat(lambda[t,1:3])
    lambda[t,1]<-equals(x[t-1],1)*tau+(1-equals(x[t-1],1))*(1-tau)/2
    lambda[t,2]<-equals(x[t-1],2)*tau+(1-equals(x[t-1],2))*(1-tau)/2
    lambda[t,3]<-equals(x[t-1],3)*tau+(1-equals(x[t-1],3))*(1-tau)/2
    
   
    prob[t]<-equals(cues[t,x[t]],1)*gamma+equals(cues[t,x[t]],-1)*(1-gamma)
    target[t]~dbern(prob[t])
    
  }
})

The issue I'm having is related to the definition of the auxiliary variable 'prob'. The idea is that prob should be separate for each particle of x. That is, it should define the probability of the target appearing to the right, as a function of the relevant arrow (according to a specific particle x) pointing right (1) or left(-1) and gamma. 
However, first, when building the model I get this warning:

running calculate on model (any error reports that follow may simply reflect missing values in model variables) ... Error in if (x1 == x2) 1 else 0 : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Second, when examining 'prob' I get the same value (0.75 or 0.25) for each column of the particles matrix  (i.e. for each time point). That is - it seems to ignore the value of x for the relevant particle, and just choose a constant value for all. 

Any help would be appreciated.
Thanks,
Isaac.

parts:
Sure. Here it is. First we generate the data, and then apply the filter. Note that now I also received the following warning:
"Warning: dynamic index out of bounds: nimEquals(cues[t, x[t]], 1) * gamma[1] + nimEquals(cues[t, x[t]], -1) * (1 - gamma[1])". 
Not sure what it means. cues is a 88*3 matrix, t goes from 2 to 88 in the for loop, and x[t] can be {1,2,3}. So I'm not sure what is the issue with the 'index out of range' here. 
(Also note that for simplicity I've fixed gamma and tau instead of giving them priors

#Generate data-----
nCues=2
nTrials=44*nCues
validity=0.75
t=1
changeT<-round(runif(nCues-1,40,48))
#changeT<-sample(c(40,48),1)
changeT<-cumsum(changeT)

genTarget=sign(runif(nTrials,-10000,10000))
genTarget[genTarget==0]<-1
relCue=rep(NA,nTrials)
opt=c(1,2,3)
relCue[1]=sample(opt,size = 1)
genCues<-matrix(rep(NA,nTrials*3),nrow=nTrials)
genCues[1,relCue[1]]<-genTarget[1]
other=c(1,2,3)
other<-other[other!=relCue[1]]
genCues[1,other]<-sample(c(-1,1),1)
genCues[1,genCues[1,]==0]<-1

relCue[t]=relCue[t-1]
  if (max(t==changeT)==1) {
    #    opt<-opt[opt!=relCue[t-1]]
    if (length(opt)>1) {relCue[t]=sample(opt,size = 1)} else {relCue[t]=opt}
  }
  valid=runif(1,0,1)
  if (valid<=validity){genCues[t,relCue[t]]<-genTarget[t]} else {genCues[t,relCue[t]]<--1*genTarget[t]}
  #other=c(1,2,3)
  #other<-other[other!=relCue[t]]
  genCues[t,-relCue[t]]<-sign(runif(2,-10000,10000))
  #  genCues[t,genCues[t,]==0]<-1
  
}

test=data.frame(genCues,genTarget,relCue)



stateSpaceCode<-nimbleCode({
  gamma<-0.75
  tau<-0.9

x[1]~dcat(lambda[1,1:3])
  lambda[1,1]<-1/3
  lambda[1,2]<-1/3
  lambda[1,3]<-1/3
  
  prob[1]<-equals(cues[1,x[1]],1)*gamma+equals(cues[1,x[1]],-1)*(1-gamma)
  
  target[1]~dbern(prob[1])
  
  for (t in 2:nTrials){
    x[t]~dcat(lambda[t,1:3])
    lambda[t,1]<-equals(x[t-1],1)*tau+(1-equals(x[t-1],1))*(1-tau)/2
    lambda[t,2]<-equals(x[t-1],2)*tau+(1-equals(x[t-1],2))*(1-tau)/2
    lambda[t,3]<-equals(x[t-1],3)*tau+(1-equals(x[t-1],3))*(1-tau)/2
    
    prob[t]<-equals(cues[t,x[t]],1)*gamma+equals(cues[t,x[t]],-1)*(1-gamma)
    target[t]~dbern(prob[t])
    
  }
})

datalist<-list(cues=as.matrix(test[,1:3]),target=as.numeric((test[,4]==1)))

inits<-list(
  gamma=0.75,
  tau=0.9
)


constants<-list(nTrials=length(datalist$target))

stateSpaceModel<-nimbleModel(code = stateSpaceCode,data = datalist,constants=constants,inits = inits)
bootstrapFilter<-buildBootstrapFilter(stateSpaceModel,nodes='prob',control=list(saveAll=T))
compiledList<-compileNimble(stateSpaceModel,bootstrapFilter)
compiledList$bootstrapFilter$run(1000)

post<-as.matrix(compiledList$bootstrapFilter$mvEWSamples)




Thanks a lot!

messages.subject: Re: Using dynamic indexing in a particle filter
parts:
Thanks for the complete example.  That makes it much easier to look at.

Regarding the incomplete initialization: stateSpaceModel$initializeInfo() reveals that x, lambda and prob are not fully initialized when the model is created.  As the message says, this is not an error, but it is letting you know.

I think the incomplete initialization is responsible for the message later, when the particle filter runs, about indices out of bounds.  So in your case, full initialization will be needed.

For you to get running, I recommend either fully initializing up to at least the first state or using the blanket approach of:
stateSpaceModel$simulate()
stateSpaceModel$calculate()

For us, I will file an issue to see if the particle filters could take a more careful initialization approach automatically in a case like this.

Regarding the unchanging values of 0.75 or 0.25 for each prob[t] throughout the particle filter run: I think you are not specifying the nodes argument as needed.  This should be a variable that contains a sequence of stochastic nodes representing the system state.  In your model I think this would be 'x'.  When I use nodes = 'x', then I do see heterogeneity in the particle sample of x values.  I believe it needs to be a stochastic node in order for the setup code to correctly determine the right sets of nodes to be simulated and/or calculated as the particle filter proceeds.

Let us know further issues.

-Perry
